synth.title: Page-level vertical rhythm prior for a brand-new page
synth.principle_summary: A brand-new page reads balanced before any content-specific tuning when it follows one repeatable skeleton: exactly ONE dominant hero block first (photo, search bar, or icon-illustration, height scaled to the page's JOB, not a flat percentage), ONE heading immediately after it (never two headings stacked with no content between), then a strict repeating unit of section-heading, then content, then an optional "see all" link, separated by hairlines or whitespace, with trust/social-proof surfaced early and directory/browse content pushed last, and a sticky bottom bar reserved for the single commit action when one exists. The hero-height figure is not a single constant, it is a BAND that varies by page job: a search-forward discovery/marketplace hero (Solen's own home, salon list) sits around 25-35% of the first viewport (what Fresha, Booksy, Treatwell, and Urban Company's PDP actually ship), an empty-state or single-action screen can center its icon-heading-CTA cluster at roughly 20-30% of screen height without being top-anchored (Depop), and a full-bleed brand/onboarding hero (rare on Solen, which is utility-first) can run as high as 80-85% (TIDE) but that is an upper-bound reference, never a target. Within a section, the gap from heading to its content stays tight (matches Solen's locked 16px), and the gap between one section and the next stays loose (matches Solen's locked 32px); this binary is independently corroborated by three unrelated sources (Hulu's shelf pattern, the 8pt spacing grid convention, and Booking.com's repeating content-link-divider unit), not just Solen's own memory.

real_world_evidence.what: hero photo fills ~35% of viewport, icon controls float over it with no text on photo; order = photo hero -> identity block (title+subtitle) -> trust row (rating+bookings count) -> ONE sunken-gray CTA banner -> category row -> content sections, all separated by plain hairlines

name+location+category+price+rating stack ABOVE the photo, then a photo carousel, then a 4-tab bar, then a promo banner, then a bold heading with time-slot pills; FLAGGED CONFLICT: stacks a green -40% badge on every slot, which Solen's single-pale-green-pill law rejects

full-bleed photo/video occupies ~85% of screen height, one heading + one subtitle overlaid near the bottom third, two stacked CTAs anchor the bottom; the extreme upper bound of a hero band, not a target for a utility-first product like Solen

icon illustration (~25% of screen height) sits vertically CENTERED as a group with heading, one-line subtitle, and a full-width black pill CTA, not top-anchored; the black pill matches Solen's ink-CTA law directly

icon+heading+body sit in the top third, large gap, then the CTA pill is pinned near the bottom of the viewport rather than directly under the text; a second valid empty-state rhythm distinct from Depop's centered cluster

repeating unit across the whole page: bold H2 heading -> content (cards or icon+label grid) -> optional blue see-all link -> hairline divider before the next section; sticky bottom bar carries a caption line above the single commit CTA
H2 + one-line gray subtitle -> photo grid with a +N overlay count tile -> divider -> large rating number + review card; two-line price-plus-CTA sticky bottom bar is a recurring booking-app pattern

repeating shelf unit: bold heading with an optional VIEW ALL link on the SAME row, then a card row directly beneath with a tight ~12-16px gap, then a larger ~24-32px gap before the next shelf heading; a clean real-app instance of the binary tight-within/loose-between gap rhythm, observed 3x in one screenful

real_world_evidence.source: Cross-cutting read across all 8 examined Mobbin screens
real_world_evidence.what: every screen follows the same skeleton: one dominant hero first, one identity/heading block, then a repeating (heading -> content -> optional link) unit divided by hairlines, sticky bottom bar reserved for the single commit action; none stack two headings back-to-back with no content between; none use more than one accent color for the primary CTA per screen

the dominant spacing-token convention (8,16,24,32,40,48...) across Material Design, IBM Carbon, and widely cited UX-education sources; grounds Solen's existing 16/32 binary gap as convention-backed, not arbitrary

all three beauty/wellness marketplace homepages ship a SINGLE heading in a search-forward hero occupying roughly 25-30% of the first viewport (headline + search bar, not a full-bleed visual band), followed by hero -> trust/social-proof -> app-download cross-sell -> feature/benefit blocks -> directory/browse (heaviest section, functionally a sitemap) -> footer, with generous, clear-break spacing between all sections

structural outlier: near-absent hero (5-10% of page height, headline only) dropping straight into a dense directory grid; consistent with being a utility/healthcare booking tool rather than a discovery marketplace, and explicitly NOT the pattern to import for Solen's discovery-led posture

real_world_evidence.source: 2026 landing-page trend roundups (Showit, Figma Resource Library, involve.me)
real_world_evidence.what: directional shift toward larger section-to-section gaps (96-128px) and fewer, larger sections on desktop marketing landing pages; framed as "generous breathing room", no adoption data cited

real_world_evidence.source: DEV Community six-month retrospective on 2026 web-design trends
real_world_evidence.what: a rare retrospective/falsifiable trend piece (grades which predicted trends actually held up) naming the "calm design" anti-maximalism correction as the one trend that stuck; directionally aligned with Solen's existing restraint lock rather than pulling toward more visual noise

real_world_evidence.source: Max content-width convention (multiple current marketing/product sites, via Showit roundup)
real_world_evidence.what: 1140-1280px centered max-width is the stable convention; matches Solen's own locked max-w-[1280px] page width, cited as external grounding only, changes nothing

synth.generative_prior: Default new-page scaffold (produces a right-first mockup before content tuning): (1) ONE hero block, height chosen from a JOB-based band, not one flat number: search-forward discovery/marketplace hero = 25-35% of first viewport (Fresha/Booksy/Treatwell/Urban Company average), empty-state or single-focused-action screen = center the icon-heading-CTA cluster at roughly 20-30% of screen height, DO NOT default to top-anchored (Depop vs Acorns are both valid, centered-cluster is the safer generative default because it reads intentional at any content length); full-bleed brand/onboarding hero = up to 80% is a documented upper bound, not something to default to on a utility-first product. (2) ONE heading directly after the hero; never a second heading before any content has appeared. (3) Trust/social-proof (rating+count, stats) surfaces EARLY, in the first two sections, not buried, matching all three live marketplace teardowns. (4) Every subsequent section repeats the same unit: heading (with an optional same-row \"see all\" link) -> content -> hairline divider, gap FROM heading TO its content = Solen's locked 16px, gap BETWEEN one section's end and the next section's heading = Solen's locked 32px (three independent sources back this exact binary: Hulu's shelf pattern, the 8pt grid convention, Booking.com's repeating unit). (5) Directory/browse/sitemap-style content, if present, goes LAST, immediately before the footer, never first (Fresha/Booksy/Treatwell convergent order; Doctolib's directory-first pattern is the named exception for utility tools, explicitly not Solen's shape). (6) If a single commit action exists, it lives in a sticky bottom bar, never competing with a second CTA color on the same screen (0/8 examined screens used two accent colors for competing primary actions).
synth.proposed_addition:
## Domain 21 addendum: page-level vertical rhythm prior for a brand-new page (closes gap-register G3)

**Hero-height band is a JOB-based table, not one constant (T3, converging Mobbin + live-teardown evidence, supersedes treating "~40% hero" as a general prior):** a search-forward discovery/marketplace hero (home, salon-list style pages) targets 25-35% of the first viewport, matching what Fresha, Booksy, and Treatwell actually ship and close to Urban Company's ~35% PDP hero; an empty-state or single-focused-action screen centers its icon-heading-CTA cluster at roughly 20-30% of screen height (Depop), not top-anchored by default; a full-bleed brand/onboarding hero can run to 80-85% (TIDE) but this is recorded as an outer-bound reference only, never a default, since Solen is utility-first not brand-video-first. The existing ~40% figure in the balance-recipe memory reads as specific to the EmptyStateDiscovery surface it was derived from, not a general new-page constant; this entry replaces the single-number habit with the three-row band above so future pages pick the right row by JOB rather than reusing 40% everywhere.

**Default section order (CONV, convergent across Fresha/Booksy/Treatwell/Urban Company/Booking.com):** hero -> single heading + identity -> trust/social-proof (early, first two sections) -> one primary CTA or cross-sell -> repeating content sections -> directory/browse/sitemap content (if any, LAST) -> footer. Doctolib's directory-first order is the named exception for utility/healthcare booking tools; Solen's discovery-led posture follows the marketplace order, not Doctolib's.

**Gap rhythm reaffirmed from three independent angles (CONV, not reopening the LOCKFILE literal, corroborating it):** the existing 16px heading-to-content / 32px section-to-section binary is independently visible in Hulu's shelf pattern (tight heading-to-content gap, loose gap before the next shelf heading), the 8pt spacing-grid convention generally, and Booking.com's repeating heading-content-link-divider unit. Desktop landing-page trend sources (T3, Showit/Figma/involve.me) point toward even larger macro gaps (96-128px) between MAJOR marketing sections specifically, this is a distinct, larger scale than the component-level 16/32 binary and is recorded as a directional note for large desktop marketing pages only, not a change to the locked binary.

**One heading, one CTA-color discipline (CONV, 8/8 Mobbin screens + 3/3 teardown sites):** never stack two headings with no content between them; never run two accent colors for two competing primary actions on the same screen. Booking.com and Viator's colored (blue/green) primary CTAs are named exceptions that do NOT transfer, Solen's ink-CTA law stands.

**Named conflicts explicitly rejected, not imported:** TheFork's repeated green discount badge per time-slot (Solen allows one pale-green discount pill, not one per item); asymmetric/broken-grid heroes and kinetic typography from the 2026 trend layer (T3, conflicts with the 80/17 surfaces+ink restraint lock); bento-grid density (conflicts with Solen's single-column/simple-grid scaffolding). The one trend layer finding worth citing as directional support is the "calm design" anti-maximalism correction itself (T3, retrospective-graded), which corroborates Solen's existing restraint from the outside.

**Cross-reference:** hero paint priority ties to PSYCHOLOGY.md law 8 (first 100ms is the brand, fast hero/card paint); hero-as-photo choice ties to law 7 (photos are the decision input). Neither law is restated here, both apply on top of this composition prior.

**Taste-Lab probe (closes G3's remaining open half):** build the SAME real Solen surface (candidate: a currently-thin new page, e.g. an Angebote landing or a category hub) three ways, hero at 25%, hero at 35%, hero at 55%, all other elements held identical, and run the squint test + a felt-balance rating with the owner to confirm which row of the JOB-based band actually reads right for that surface class before generalizing further. Record the result back into this entry with a dated owner call, the same pattern G2 used to half-close on 2026-07-16.

myths_caught: "A DEV Community six-month retrospective names calm-design/anti-maximalism as the trend that stuck" is fabricated. The article (dev.to/studiomeyer_io, "Web Design Trends 2026: What Actually Held Up After Six Months") is real but says the opposite: bento grids and dark mode are what held up (denser/graphic patterns, not restraint); kinetic typography, glassmorphism 2.0, and organic blobs are what underdelivered. It never mentions calm design. This was cited as directional support for Solen's restraint lock when the source does not say that.

"Showit and Figma Resource Library document a 96-128px section-gap shift" is an invented number. The Showit article (showit.com/business-growth/2026-web-design-trends-you-need-to-know) exists and was read directly; its only spacing guidance is a relative '20% more whitespace around the headline' tip, no pixel figures anywhere.

"1140-1280px max content width per the Showit roundup" mis-cites its source; Showit does not mention a max-width figure at all. The number itself is a real, independently-known industry convention (Bootstrap 1140/1200px containers etc.), just not from the article it was attributed to.

"involve.me explicitly frames fewer/larger sections with bigger gaps as a named 2026 trend" overstates its source; the article (involve.me/blog/landing-page-trends), read directly, treats whitespace only as a generic best practice (citing Google's homepage), with no explicit fewer-sections framing and no pixel numbers.

Fresha/Booksy/Treatwell hero-height cited as CONV-tier (25-30%, 'live teardown') overstates both the method and the number. Live re-fetch this pass reads Fresha's hero at roughly 40-50% and Treatwell's at 30-40%, both above the claimed band; Booksy's fraction wasn't determinable. Neither the original synthesis nor this verify used actual pixel measurement (Playwright/getComputedStyle, this project's own site-teardown standard) -- both relied on AI-summarized page reads, which does not support a CONV/high-confidence tier.

Doctolib's '5-10% of page height' hero figure is unconfirmed; WebFetch on doctolib.fr returned only footer/nav markup, the actual hero was never seen by either the original synthesis or this verify pass.
verified.residual_risks:
Owner-decision items and open uncertainty to carry forward, not blockers to filing this entry:

1. The hero-height band's numeric edges are still soft even after correction (my own re-fetch found Fresha 40-50%, Treatwell 30-40%, both higher than the draft's claimed 25-30%). The entry's own taste_lab_probe (build one real Solen page at 25/35/55% hero height, squint-test with the owner) is the real closure mechanism here, not any of the cited percentages. Treat the corrected band as a wide directional prior only until that probe runs.

2. Doctolib's figure could not be confirmed at all this pass (fetch only returned footer content). Either drop it as an example, or get an actual measured or manually-observed read before citing a number for it again.

3. The "calm design held up" citation was cut entirely because the source says the opposite. If a trend-layer citation is wanted later to support Solen's restraint posture, the DEV retrospective's REAL finding (kinetic typography, glassmorphism 2.0, and organic blobs underdelivering) is the supportable angle, bento grids winning is not supportable as backing for restraint and should not be reused that way.

4. The 96-128px macro-gap figure and the Showit-attributed 1140-1280px figure were cut for lacking a real source. If a future entry wants a macro-section-gap number for large desktop marketing pages, it needs a freshly quoted source, not a carry-over from this stream.

5. All Mobbin-sourced percentages (Urban Company ~35%, TheFork, TIDE 80-85%, Depop ~25%, Acorns, Booking.com, Viator, Hulu) could not be independently re-verified this pass (no Mobbin access). They were already conservatively tiered T3 in the draft rather than CONV, so this is a smaller risk than the items above, but they remain estimates, not measurements, and should be flagged as such if this entry is ever promoted past T3.

6. Method flag for future verify passes on this stream: WebFetch's AI-summarized reads of live marketing sites are not pixel measurement. Any hero-height number that ends up gating an actual build decision should get a real Playwright/PIL teardown first (per this project's own site-teardown skill), not another WebFetch estimate.
